newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-C&W takes control of Australia's Optus.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-C&W takes control of Australia's Optus.

text.p: Cable and Wireless, Britain's second biggest telecoms company, said on Tuesday it planned to take financial as well as managerial control of Australian carrier Optus Communications.

C&W, which already owned a 24.5 percent stake in Optus, ended weeks of speculation by announcing it had agreed to buy another 24.5 percent stake from America's BellSouth Corp for 445 million pounds ($740.6 million).

If it wins a regulatory green light from the Australian government, C&W then plans to raise its stake in Australia's second carrier to around 51.5 percent by excercising options at a price of A$565 million.
Optus plans to issue 298.9 million options. Each option allows C&W to buy one newly-issued Optus share at an average estimated price of A$1.89 ($1.42) over a three-year period.
This will take C&W's stake to 55 percent initially. But a previous options issue after Optus merged with the pay television and local telephony group Optus Vision will dilute the stake, C&W said.
"This is a unique opportunity for us to manage Optus and add shareholder value," said C&W's chief executive Richard Brown.
Analysts welcomed the deal which allows C&W to take control of a company in a key telecoms hub in the booming Asia-Pacific region at a price they said was full -- but fair.
Andrew Harrington, telecoms analyst at Salomon Brothers, said that C&W was paying a price at the top-end of the acceptable range.

But Harrington believes that ownership of assets is key as international telecoms companies jostle for prime positions to offer communications services to high margin, multi-national corporate customers.

"I think it's a great deal for Cable and Wireless. It really does enhance C&W as a strategic asset owner. It will now control two of the three most important Asia-Pacific telecoms hubs -- Hong Kong, Singapore and Australia -- once this deal goes ahead."
Although C&W has no controlling asset in Singapore, it is part of the MobileOne consortium which bidding for a fixed licence to enhance its mobile interests.
It also retains a slim majority stake in its most lucative asset, Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, despite the British handover of the island to China -- at least for the time being.
News of the Optus deal helped lift C&W's shares 17-1/2 PENCE to 570p by 1510 GMT with few analysts believing the Australian government would baulk at allowing C&W to take over Optus.
C&W said it planned to meet with government officials "in due course" to discuss its hopes for a relaxation of rules limiting foreign shareholders to 49 percent of Australian companies.

As part of its deal with BellSouth, Cable and Wireless said it would transfer to the American group its 22.3 percent stake in OCCEL, the mobile operator in western Colombia -- subject to that company's agreement.

"We have decided to dig our roots deeper into Australia where we can offer our customers a full range of integrated services, and plan to exit from a dilutive wireless business in Columbia, where we cannot," Brown said.
C&W has already effective management control of Optus after former C&W executive Peter Howell-Davies was appointed Optus chief executive earlier this month.
His predecessor, Ziggy Switkowski, resigned after a year of rising losses at Optus's pay television operations.

"As a high growth, fully integrated telecommunications, information and entertainment company Optus fits well with our view of the future," said Brown. "Optus is already a successful business, growing market share in a highly competitive Australian market.

"More hard work lies ahead but, now that we can manage the company, we can apply our unrivalled experience in broadband communications around the world," he added. ($ = 1.328 Australian Dollars) ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
